details.summary: This is a flavorful, fiber-packed, and highly appealing breakfast that perfectly captures the book's dual-condition dietary philosophy. However, minor ingredient adjustments (dropping the added salt and swapping one egg yolk for a white) are required to bring the sodium and saturated fat strictly within the target nutrient tier ceilings.

dimensions.feedback: Classic Mexican-American flavors work wonderfully together; the earthy beans, creamy avocado, and bright pico de gallo provide a perfectly balanced, savory profile.
Every listed ingredient is used in the instructions, and no surprise ingredients are introduced.

Instructions are excellent. They provide time ranges, precise visual doneness cues (e.g., 'soft, fluffy curds', 'warmed through and slightly crisp'), and reminders to check early to prevent overcooking.
The recipe aligns perfectly with the stated Mexican-American style, delivering a wholesome, quick take on huevos rancheros.
Toasting tortillas in a dry skillet and wilting spinach into mashed beans are standard, effective stovetop techniques that match the equipment constraints perfectly.
Nutrition values are highly plausible for the ingredients listed. The high sodium flag is expected given the combination of added kosher salt and store-bought pico de gallo.
The title accurately reflects the dish, and the intro highlights its protein and fiber assets in an encouraging, practical tone without making any banned health claims.
Highly appealing. It offers fantastic textural variety (crunchy pepitas, crisp tortillas, creamy beans, fluffy eggs) and bold flavors for a satisfying morning meal.

An excellent example of eating for both conditions: it provides high protein, substantial fiber from beans and whole-grain corn, and leans on healthy fats (avocado, olive oil, pepitas) instead of processed breakfast meats.
Perfectly zero added sugar. The complex carbohydrates (50.5g) coming from corn tortillas and beans sit ideally in the target window, providing sustained energy.

The recipe exceeds the chapter's 'main' nutrient tier ceilings for sodium (757mg vs 550mg limit) and saturated fat (5.3g vs 5.0g limit). Fix this by omitting the 1/8 tsp kosher salt entirely (let the pico de gallo season the dish) and changing the egg ratio to 3 whole eggs and 3 egg whites to safely duck under the saturated fat ceiling.
Easily achievable within 30 minutes from start to finish. All ingredients are standard supermarket staples, and the single-skillet sequence is highly practical for a busy morning.

dimensions.feedback: Classic Mexican-American breakfast flavors are well-balanced; earthy cumin, rich beans, eggs, and creamy avocado work perfectly together.
Every listed ingredient is properly integrated into the instructions.
Excellent instructions. Every step includes accurate time ranges and clear visual doneness cues (e.g., 'golden and fragrant', 'pliable and lightly toasted').
Accurately represents Mexican-American flavor profiles, ingredients, and techniques.
The sequential single-skillet method is highly suitable, keeping prep logical and cleanup minimal.
The computed nutrition values are completely consistent with the stated ingredients and quantities.
The title highlights the hero ingredients, and the intro uses warm, practical language focused on steady energy without any banned medical claims.
A very appetizing, colorful, and texturally diverse savory breakfast.
Perfectly aligns with the dietary spine: leverages plant and egg protein, immense dietary fiber from beans, and healthy monounsaturated fats from avocado and olive oil.

The recipe overshoots the breakfast chapter's 55g carbohydrate ceiling, landing at 64g. Additionally, 3/4 cup of mashed beans per person is quite thick for just two small tortillas. Reduce the pinto beans from 1.5 cups (255g) to 1 cup (170g). This will improve the bean-to-tortilla ratio and bring the carbohydrates cleanly into the 45-55g target window.
Easily completed in under 25 minutes from a cold start using everyday supermarket ingredients and a single skillet.
